Appellant has preferred this Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, assailing the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.02.2011 passed by the learned IVth Additional Sessions Judge (Fast Tract Court) to the Court of X th Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal(MP) in Sessions Trial No.27/2009 (State of MP Vs. After completion of investigation,
charge-sheet has been filed before the competent Court.

Charges under Section 363, 366- A. 376(1)
of IPC were framed against the appellant(s)/accused.
Accused has refuted the charge and claimed to be tried.
Statements of the witnesses were recorded.

After recording the statements of prosecution witnesses and appreciating the evidence led by the parties, learned Trial Court found the appellant guilty for commission of aforementioned offence and convicted & sentenced him as mentioned preceding paragraph No.1.

sentences.text: 1 preferred this criminal appeal before this Court.

3. During the pendency of this appeal, I.A. No.3732/2017 & I.A. No.3733/2017-applications seeking leave to compound offence as also for compromise have been filed stating that dispute between the parties have been resolved and they have entered into compromise with no intention to pursue the matter further.
The applications are duly supported by affidavit of complainant Pappu Kabir Panthi.
4. Vide order dated 18.09.2025, matter was referred to the Registrar (Judicial-II) of this Court for verification of compromise.

Registrar (Judicial-II) in compliance of this Court's order has verified the aforesaid compromise and has submitted the report dated 22.09.2025 wherein it is mentioned that parties have amicably settled their dispute NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 3 CRA-530-2011 and have arrived at compromise on their own free will & volition and without any threat, inducement or coercion to settle their dispute and the compromise is voluntarily.
Appellant/accused and complainant have been duly identified by their respective counsel.
5. The purpose of compromise is to maintain peace and harmony in the relations.
Section 320 of CrPC deals with compounding of offence.

6. On the basis of the verification report dated 22.09.2025 furnished by Registrar (Judicial-II), this Court is satisfied that the parties have arrived at a compromise on their free-will and volition.
However, the appellant was convicted and sentenced for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC, which is non-compoundable offence.

7. At the very outset, learned counsel for the appellant submits that he does not want to challenge the conviction of the appellant recorded under Section 363 of IPC by the Trial Court, but has prayed for reduction of jail sentence.

It is submitted that the incident had taken place in the year 2008 i.e.
almost 17 years ago.
It is further submitted that applicant is the first offender.
It is further submitted that appellant was in custody from 06.12.2008 to 06.01.2009 (32 dyas) during trial.
He has already served out the jail sentence from the date of judgment i.e. 07.02.2011 to 01.07.2011 i.e. the date of suspension of his jail sentence (145 days).
Thus; in total, appellant has suffered the incarceration period approximately six months so far in this case.
It is further submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 4 CRA-530-2011 compromise has already been entered between the parties and parties have amicably settled their dispute.
Therefore, it is prayed that appellant's jail sentence may be reduced/modified to the extent of period already undergone by him.

8. Learned counsel for the State has supported the findings recorded by the Trial Court and has submitted that after appreciating the evidence produced by the prosecution, the Trial Court has rightly found the appellant guilty for the aforesaid offence and has prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10. Though, the appellant have not assailed the findings of conviction under Section 363 of IPC on merits and has confined the submissions only to the quantum of sentence on the basis of the Ravi Kumar Panthi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158603569/
2 compromise entered between the parties; this Court, is nonetheless under a legal obligation to scrutinize the correctness and sanctity of the conviction recorded by the trial Court.

sentences.text: On this aspect, I have carefully perused the judgment of the trial Court and the evidence adduced during trial.
The prosecution case is not only corroborated by the testimony of the witnesses, but also stands duly supported by other materials placed on record.

The trial Court, while appreciating the entire evidence in its proper perspective, has arrived at a well-reasoned finding of guilt against NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 5 CRA-530-2011 the appellant.

Upon independent reappraisal, I find that the conclusion so recorded by the trial Court is based on cogent reasoning and does not suffer from any perversity or illegality warranting interference by this Court.
Accordingly, the findings of conviction of the appellant under Section 363 of IPC are hereby upheld.
11. Turning to the point of compromise, it is also significant to note that the compromise has been filed at the stage of appeal before this Court.

On this aspect, it would be relevant to note the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ishwar Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh [AIR 2009 SC 675], wherein the Apex Court has observed as under:
"15.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our considered opinion, it would not be appropriate to order compounding of an offence not compoundable under the code ignoring and keeping aside statutory provisions.

In our judgment, however, limited submission of the learned counsel for the appellant deserves consideration that while imposing substantive sentence, the factum of compromise between the parties is indeed a relevant circumstances which,
the Court may keep in mind."

12. On this point, the view of Hon'ble Apex Court in the Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan versus State of Kerala reported in AIR 2017 Supreme Court 1745 is also worth referring in the context of this case as under:-
"10.

In series of decisions i.e. Bharath Singh vs. State of M.P. and Ors., 1990 (Supp)
SCC 62, Ramlal vs. State of J & K, (1999) 2 SCC 213, Puttaswamy vs. State of Karnataka and Anr, (2009) 1 SCC 71 1, this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 6 CRA-530-2011 allowed the parties to compound the offence even though the offence is a non-compoundable depending on the facts and circumstances of each case.

sentences.text: In some cases this Court while imposing the fine amount reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

11. What emerges from the above is that even if an offence is not compoundable within the scope of Section 320 of Code of Criminal Procedure the Court may, in view of the compromise arrive at between the parties, reduce the sentence imposed while maintaining the conviction."
13.

In the case of Murali vs. State; (2021) 1 SCC 726, Hon'ble the Apex Court has held that the fact of amicable settlement/compromise between the parties can be a relevant factor for the purpose of reduction in quantum of sentence of convicts even in serious non-compoundable offences.

sentences.text: In the present case, it is seen that the parties have entered into compromise and have amicably settled their dispute, which has been duly verified.

It is true that the offence under Section 363 of IPC is not compoundable under the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973; therefore,
the compromise cannot be allowed.

However, as held by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in aforementioned case laws, in exceptional circumstances, considering the voluntary settlement between the parties, the Court may give effect to such compromise at the stage of final disposal of appeal and further that where parties have amicably resolved NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 7 CRA-530-2011 their disputes and the complainant has unequivocally supported the compromise; the Court may, in the interest of justice and to maintain social harmony,
modify the relief suitably by reducing the substantive sentence.

15. Having taken into consideration the above submissions and the fact that the compromise has voluntarily been entered into between the parties and the complainant(s)/injured has no objection to compounding the offence and also considering the nature of the accusation, the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellant and also the fact that appellant is facing the agony for the last 17 years as the incident had taken place in the year 2008, I am of the considered opinion that the ends of justice would be met if the sentence of imprisonment awarded to the appellant under Section 363 of IPC is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
16. Thus, the conviction of the appellant under Section 363 of I P C as recorded by the trial Court, is hereby affirmed.
However, the appellant's sentence as awarded by the Trial Court for the alleged offence is modified and reduced to the period already undergone by him so far.
The fine amount, if not already deposited, shall be deposited within a period of two months from today.
However, if the appellant fails to pay the fine amount within the stipulated time, he would suffer the punishment as awarded by the trial court in default of payment of fine.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50988 8 CRA-530-2011 17.
Appellant is on bail.
His bail bonds shall stand discharged.
18. The order of the Trial Court pertaining the seized property is hereby affirmed.
19. Learned Trial Court is directed to ensure the aforesaid compliance.
20. The present criminal appeal is disposed of to the extent indicated herein-above.
21. Record of Trial Court, if available, along with copy of this order be sent to the Court concerned for information and necessary action.
22. Certified copy as per rules.
